prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: first-person castle exploration game environment. ONE finished landscape 1536x1024 image, 3:2, full bleed.
Input image 1 is an ARCHITECTURAL REFERENCE ONLY: the user's approved courtyard-v2, with pale warm-gray limestone, solid two-storey wings, a substantial round crenellated tower, a square tower visible behind the wing, dark unified slate roofs, large stone buttresses, a small unroofed stone well and a pointed garden gateway. Generate a NEW tower-top viewpoint of this same castle, not an edit of the courtyard camera and not a copy of its ground-level framing. Preserve its material identity and recognizable fortified construction.
USER CORRECTIONS: the previous lookout made the castle look like ordinary residential buildings, and trees grew densely right against it as if the castle were inside a forest. Correct BOTH decisively. This image must immediately read as a prosperous LORD'S FORTIFIED CASTLE with imposing stone mass, and it must stand in OPEN GROUNDS with woodland clearly far away.
VIEWPOINT: standing at human eye level INSIDE a tower-top terrace, behind a waist-high crenellated stone parapet. Look diagonally across the castle's inner courtyard and roofscape, then outward across open land. A slim strip of terrace paving and heavy chamfered parapet with two broad crenellations occupy the bottom fifth; keep the view open above the low central coping. The tower staircase is behind the camera; no additional navigation exit. This is a natural view from a real inhabited tower, not a drone, isometric map, bird's-eye floor plan, detached fantasy citadel or impossibly high mountain lookout.
CASTLE ARCHITECTURE IS THE PRIMARY SUBJECT in the foreground and middle ground. Show the reference's tall thick limestone masses and TWO-STOREY residential wings as parts of a coherent FORTIFIED enclosure. Visually emphasize a dominant broad square stone tower block rising above the wing roofs, battlemented parapets, massive load-bearing walls, deep window embrasures, strong projecting buttresses, heavy stone corbels, and a substantial stone curtain wall tied into the buildings. The square tower is based on the partly visible square tower in the reference; make its weight and defensive skyline legible from this new angle. One robust rounded corner bastion can anchor the far side, clearly physically integrated into the masonry rather than a tiny ornamental roof turret. Do not show the same tower the viewer is standing on from an external aerial angle. Keep an inhabited lord's castle scale, dignified and strong, with a clear hierarchy of tower, curtain wall and lower residential wings. No sprawling imperial palace, gigantic citadel, extra rows of apartment blocks or dozens of towers.
Keep broad DARK CHARCOAL SLATE ROOF planes subordinate to the strong crenellated stone silhouette. Use very few understated chimneys and no cute dormer rows, little residential gables, many cottage roofs or exposed timber-eave trim. Inner courtyard windows may retain the reference's restrained pointed Gothic design; outer wall faces have sparse deeply recessed smaller windows with large expanses of uninterrupted thick stone. Avoid a facade consisting entirely of giant glass windows or repetitive domestic storeys.
Below the viewer, glimpse the same broad paved inner COURTYARD, several dozen paces across, spacious enough to feel part of a true castle. At one side, a small UNROOFED circular pale-stone well with the reference's simple iron hoisting frame; no well canopy. One broad pointed stone gate leads to the adjacent private garden. Show the GARDEN as a sheltered smaller enclosure with a modest lawn, rose-clothed stone walls, layered pink-white flower masses including cosmos, a few stone seats and ONE ornamental tree. Keep the garden a secondary intimate detail; do not transform the entire castle into a garden complex or show giant flowers in the tower foreground.
CRITICAL OPEN LAND: immediately OUTSIDE the castle's outer wall, show a BROAD, CONTINUOUS, CLEARLY VISIBLE APRON OF OPEN SUNLIT GRASSLAND extending outward for several castle widths before any dense woodland begins. This open ground must be visible from the base of the enclosing wall through the middle distance on at least the right half of the view; do not hide it entirely behind the buildings. A natural mix of short grass, muted meadow greens and subtle earth tones, gently undulating low ground, only a few widely scattered shrubs or individual small trees. NO dense trees at the foot of the walls, no surrounding ring of mature tree crowns, no forest canopy filling the middle distance. The dense FOREST is a restrained narrow distant horizon band separated from the castle by all that open ground, softened by atmospheric haze; individual near trees must not visually engulf the castle. Do not make this a clearing tightly encircled by woods.
Clear pale blue sky with soft clouds, luminous afternoon sunlight on warm-gray stone, natural shadows and tactile weathering; match the fine realistic environmental painting of the reference. Strong coherent rigid architecture and believable perspective, cared for and inhabited.
Only castle roofs, court, garden, open grounds and DISTANT woodland. Do not add a village, town, farms, crop fields, named road, river, lake, moat, coast, mountains, cliffs, another castle on the horizon, flags, heraldry, people, animals, labels, text, UI, arrows, hotspots or watermark. Architecture and visible open space must carry the grandeur.
